items.title: Wilbert Tillman Interview, 1961-08-15
items.q: So I started taking lessons from the Lewis Demand, and I still was playing my clarinet

ctx.x: That after you left Jack Caring?

Oh yeah, Jack was dead then. Yeah, that was in the late years. That was around in the thirties. Around in the thirties, yeah. And, um... After, after we... made up our own little band, well, we wasn't getting much work because we wasn't known at that time, but I still was working with other bands. Now, my first brass band that I would say that I was really a member, you see, because I had started learning trumpet then, but I was taking lessons on the Lewis Demand, I was trying to get away from the reed. items.title: Wilbert Tillman Interview, 1966-01-20
items.q: I'm the one who got Lewis the man in the WPA band.

ctx.x: I never met him. I never met Lewis the man, neither. Yeah, I was.

I'm the one who got Lewis the man in the WPA band. In fact, I was the first trumpet player in the WPA band, could play anything that people could understand. There was a bunch of them in there. But Gilbert had the band then. Gilbert had the band way before Martina came. And what Gilbert did, he got in there and he'd taken everybody who said he was a musician. Then he classified him. He classified him just like a school, like it started from first grade on up. And he rated him according to their plan abilities.
